Weight gain or loss is an energy balance. IN all mass/energy transfer systems, there is a simple governing equation.

Accumulation = Inputs - Outputs +/- RXN

So basically if we call accumulation (positive or negative) body weight, the sole input is the number of calories you eat, the output is your poop, and the reaction term is calories burned. Calories burned is the summation of your base metabolic rate (BMR) (calories burned to maintain body function, heal, etc) and calories burned through motion. You can calculate how many calories you eat, how many calories you burn, your BMR, AND your rate of weight loss. This means you are left with estimating how many calories you are pooping out. Once you have done that, you can compare that number to the mass flow rate of poop coming out of your body and see if that value is reasonable.

Most likely you are either under-counting calories or you're pooping a lot.
